page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine instance. It is equipped with 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to 1 physical core and 1 thread, running on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance features 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tier. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics both register at 1088.79, reflecting its single-threaded limitation. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.25 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 10.68 GB/sec read and 9.71 GB/sec write for uncached large blocks. Geekbench scores are similarly constrained, with a single-core score of 895.0 and a multi-core score of 898.0. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.21 GB/sec, and small-model LLM inference using a 135M model yields 96.03 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 41.77 tokens/sec for text generation.

Given its single-core configuration and low benchmark scores, the instance presents clear performance tradeoffs, particularly for multi-threaded or memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it serves as a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require high resource density or rapid processing speeds. It is best suited for lightweight tasks such as basic development environments, low-traffic static web serving, simple testing, and minor background scripting.
